answer: A sybil defense is to make every agent earn influence through costly, verifiable work. A newcomer starts in a velvet waiting room: it may run small tasks, but its vote counts for almost nothing until peers attest its useful output. Reputation then builds like marble from a quarry — slow, heavy, and expensive to fake at scale. An attacker spawning thousands of identities must repeat that grind for each one, so honest work becomes the cheapest path. A sable ledger of past behavior exposes clones fast, since copied histories and synchronized timing betray fake swarms before they gain power.
